newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada June housing starts fall 7.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada June housing starts fall 7.9 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts fell by 7.9 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 140,200 units from an unrevised 152,300 units in May, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Wednesday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts of 155,300 units.
Actual housing starts fell to 14,948 in June from a revised 16,438 (16,435) the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said that although housing starts in June was 7.9 percent lower than May, housing starts remained ahead of last year's pace of 134,900.

"This lull in new construction mirrors the pause in existing home sales the previous month," CMHC economist Michel Laurence said in a statement. "Low mortgage rates pulled housing markets higher early in the year, and we expect a similar impact later this year as a result of job creation."
The provincial estimates are for centers with more than 10,000 people. The other area estimates are for centers with less than 10,000.
